headline: The steroid risk list
body: Everyone knows about the liver and the heart.
punch: The brain is on that list too and almost nobody says so.

headline: The usual harm profile
body: Reproductive suppression, liver strain, kidney load, cardiac remodelling. That's the standard catalogue people repeat.
punch: The central nervous system is rarely included in it.

headline: Applied directly
body: Anabolic androgenic steroids showed direct neurotoxic effects in primary rat cortical cell cultures — the cells themselves, not downstream of hormonal changes.
punch: Direct toxicity, not a secondary consequence.

headline: Why that matters
body: Most AAS side effects are reversible on cessation. Neurons are among the least replaceable cells you have, and the developing brain is still organising.
punch: The reversibility assumption doesn't transfer to every tissue.

headline: And the age problem
body: Anyone using these to affect height by definition still has open growth plates — which means an adolescent brain that is still structurally maturing.
punch: The population targeting height is the population least able to absorb this.

headline: The evidence limits
body: This is cell culture. Concentrations in a dish are not doses in a person, and cortical cultures are not a behaving brain.
punch: In vitro toxicity is a signal, not a measured human risk.

headline: But note the direction
body: Nobody has run the study showing adolescent AAS use is neurologically safe either. The absence of evidence runs both ways and only one side gets mentioned.
punch: Unstudied is not the same as cleared.

headline: What to take from it
body: Add the CNS to the risk list when you see one. A harm catalogue that stops at the organs people find easy to discuss is an incomplete catalogue.
punch: Incomplete risk lists are how bad decisions look reasonable.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
